headline: South Asia: War in the Gulf
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: War in the Gulf.
- Western Russia: Russia attacks Ukraine with 170 drones overnight; 147 of them downed.
- Persian Gulf Region: Israel security forces kill terrorist who kidnapped Noa Argamani on Oct. 7 in weekend strikes.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
The United States-based software engineer accused of causing the leak of videos and photographs of a sexual encounter with a Jamaican attorney has lost a multimillion-dollar home in St Ann, which has been sold to settle a judgment handed down by the Supreme Court. Rodrick Brown, who resides in New York City, could possibly lose a second apartment as the attorney, Kimberley Facey, has filed documents in court seeking to recover millions of dollars in legal costs she incurred in pursuing the lawsuit against him.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russia attacks Ukraine with 170 drones overnight; 147 of them downed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russia attacks Ukraine with 170 drones overnight; 147 of them downed.
Russia attacked Ukraine with 170 strike drones overnight on 26-27 September. Ukrainian air defence downed 147 UAVs, while strikes were recorded at 18 locations.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Person killed in Russian attacks on Odesa, two others injured.
One person was killed and two others injured in a Russian attack on Odesa on the evening of 26 September. Emergency crews are dealing with the aftermath of the strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russians strike head office of Ukraine's mobile telecommunications operator.
A Russian drone strike damaged the Kyivstar head office on 27 September, as attacks continue targeting Ukraine's telecom and data centre infrastructure.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Lithuania warns of evacuation challenges in event of Russian attack.
Lithuanian municipalities bordering Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad Oblast have warned of transport, traffic and communications challenges during a potential mass evacuation in the event of a Russian attack.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Five men arrested on terrorism offenses near UK airbase used for US strikes on Iran.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: Five men arrested on terrorism offenses near UK airbase used for US strikes on Iran.
Britain authorized the U.S. to use the base for “defensive” strikes on Iran earlier this year.
- Politico Europe, 21 hours ago: Germany’s Wadephul meets Russia’s Lavrov amid tensions over ‘escalation’.
The German foreign minister blames Moscow for the Leipzig drone attack but welcomes the G20 invite to Vladimir Putin

AFRICA

- Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: Israel security forces kill terrorist who kidnapped Noa Argamani on Oct. 7 in weekend strikes.

Ayatollah Mohsen Heidari Alekasir also denied the claim that Iran’s former supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, had recommended his son to serve as his successor.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Why Iran's new push for a deal to end the war appears to be stalling - analysis.
Iran proposed a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for a seven-day ceasefire, but the US seems uninterested as it wants something more to show from six months of conflict.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Suicide bombing in northwest Pakistan kills at least 12.
A vehicle laden with explosives rammed into a roadside checkpoint in Pakistan, killing at least a dozen people.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Taekwondo Association of Malawi to Hold Awareness Games in Blantyre.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 days ago: Malawi: Taekwondo Association of Malawi to Hold Awareness Games in Blantyre.
[Nyasa Times] The Taekwondo Association of Malawi (TAM) has organised awareness games to take place on Saturday, 26 September, at Chichiri Shopping Mall car park from 9am to 12:30pm.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 days ago: Malawi: Prophet Kambale's Life International Church Marks a Decade With Groundbreaking Ceremony.
[Nyasa Times] There is a particular kind of energy that builds around a church anniversary when the milestone is not simply looking backwards but breaking ground on something new. That was the atmosphere at Mbinzi Secondary School Hall in Area 3, Lilongwe, where Life International Church (LIC), founded by Prophet Amos Kambale, marked a decade of ministry with a two-day Total Transformation Conference that doubled as the launch of its next chapter altogether.
Africa: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: War in the Gulf.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: War in the Gulf.
THE war that the US and Israel imposed on Iran this year has failed to achieve any of the objectives that the two countries had intended. The declared purpose was to prevent Iran from building a nuclear weapon. A fact-check indicates that Iran had kept its civil nuclear programme under IAEA safeguards. It had also willingly agreed to a nuclear deal in 2015. It was President Donald Trump who pulled the US out of the deal in 2018 and re-engaged with Iran in his second term under a “maximum pressure” campaign.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 17 hours ago: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said. Separately, two rescue workers were killed and another was injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast. DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.

Kelsey Mitchell highlights the substantial influence of rising stars Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese in the WNBA. She believes their presence has significantly elevated the visibility of women's basketball. Advocating against gatekeeping, Mitchell argues that it limits growth potential for all players. The synergy between Mitchell and Clark has proven beneficial for the Indiana Fever, bolstering their offensive strategy.

Ukraine is launching a new "Army of Robots", the country's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov announced on Saturday, as the country steps up its push to bring more machines into warfare to minimise the loss of human lives on the frontlines.
